report.summary: Classifier strongly identifies this frame as Address. The setup shows a reverse spine tilt (spine leaning toward the target) with the trail shoulder higher than the lead shoulder — both notable deviations from typical pro driver setup and likely to promote a downward/inside strike on a tee'd driver.

key_deviations.explanation: Negative value indicates the spine is tilting toward the target (reverse spine tilt) rather than the recommended tilt away from the target for a driver.
Trail (right) shoulder is outside the pro range and is higher relative to the lead shoulder, which matches the 'trail shoulder higher than lead shoulder' detection signal for reverse spine tilt.

coaching_recommendations: Create a slight tilt away from the target at address: raise the lead shoulder so the lead shoulder sits about 5–10° higher than the trail shoulder (pre-sets an upward driver strike). Drill: hold a club along the shoulders and check the angle in a mirror or video — aim for that small tilt away from the target.

Check and correct shoulder alignment: lay a club on the ground parallel to the target line and ensure the shoulder line is parallel to that reference. Drill: practice setting up to a wall or chair so the lead shoulder does not extend farther forward than the trail shoulder.

report.summary: Frame is classified as Toe-up with high confidence. There is a notable loss of spine angle (more upright than expected) that appears to continue from the Address position, and the shoulder line is high/rotated in a way that commonly accompanies an open clubface at toe-up (shaft/face inference estimated from lead-arm pose).

key_deviations.explanation: Upper body has straightened (loss of forward bend) relative to typical pros at Toe-up — indicates early loss of posture during the backswing.
Left shoulder appears higher/rotated than typical at Toe-up; this geometry often accompanies an open clubface when the shaft is horizontal (shaft/face estimate from lead-arm proxy).

coaching_recommendations: Maintain hip flexion and "stay in your posture" through the backswing — cue: keep your belt buckle pointed at the ball. Drill: make controlled half-swings with an alignment stick or foam noodle pressed between your back and a wall; losing contact signals loss of spine angle (from 'Early loss of spine angle').

Allow natural forearm rotation with a neutral grip and a one-piece takeaway to prevent the face fanning open. Drill: practice arriving at Toe-up and check the leading edge — aim for the leading edge to be within ~15° of vertical (from 'Open clubface at toe-up').

Because the clubface/shaft angle here is estimated from the lead-arm proxy (confidence ~0.63), verify clubface orientation visually: check the toe/leading edge at P2 in a mirror or slow-motion video to confirm whether the face is open and use the toe-up drill above to train the correct feel (from 'Open clubface at toe-up').

report.summary: The frame at Finish shows a notable mismatch in spine angle compared with pro norms: the torso is tipped in the opposite direction of typical pro finishes and the value is more extreme than the earlier Address and Toe-up findings, suggesting this posture pattern carried through the swing. Shoulders and hips are within typical ranges, so the primary concern is the spine/rotation pattern rather than hip rotation or obvious shoulder tilt.

key_deviations.explanation: Spine angle is well outside the pro p25–p75 range (more forward/tilted than typical), indicating the torso is not in the rotated/upright finish most pros show. This can allow the arms to finish the swing independently of body rotation (an arms-only finish) and appears connected to the similar negative spine angles noted earlier at Address and Toe-up.

coaching_recommendations: Turn the body first, arms second — cue: “lead with your chest, not your hands.” (Drill: make full turns with just the torso, no club, then add the arms.)
Practice no-ball swings focused on reaching a high, balanced finish — think of the target rather than the ball to avoid decelerating through impact and producing a short/low finish.
Work on balance and a stable base: slightly widen your stance and practice slow swings holding the finish for three seconds to expose and correct any loss of balance.

report.summary: This frame is classified as Finish (confidence 0.94). Compared with pro norms the torso is notably less rotated and the spine is more upright/extended than typical at the finish — a pattern consistent with an "arms-only" finish. This matches earlier frames (address/toe-up) that already showed reduced spine tilt, suggesting the body never fully rotated through the shot.

key_deviations.explanation: Spine is much more upright/extended than the pro range at P8, indicating the golfer has stood up or lost forward tilt through the shot which reduces effective body rotation and can shorten the follow-through.
Shoulder angle is far outside the typical pro range, consistent with minimal torso rotation at the finish — the arms appear to have swung up around a relatively unrotated body (an arms-only finish).

coaching_recommendations: Turn the body first, arms second — cue: “lead with your chest, not your hands.” Practice slow torso-only rotations (no club) to feel the chest carry the arms, then reintroduce the club.
Make practice swings with no ball, focusing on reaching a high, balanced finish aimed at the target (think target, not the ball) to discourage a short/arms-only follow-through.
If balance is unstable, widen your athletic base and perform slow-motion swings holding the finish for 3 seconds until you can consistently maintain a balanced finish.

report.summary: High-confidence classification: Finish. The frame shows a notable lack of body rotation at the finish — spine tilt is −8.1° (pros typically 10.5–17.2°) and the shoulders are markedly outside the pro range — a pattern consistent with an arms-only or short/low finish. These finish deviations are consistent with the earlier spine/shoulder issues at Address and Toe-up, suggesting under-rotation is persisting through the swing.

key_deviations.explanation: The torso is tilted forward/away from the pro range at the finish, indicating the body has not rotated and extended into the follow-through as expected.
The right shoulder angle is well outside the typical pro range, consistent with the arms carrying the club while the torso has under-rotated (an arms-only finish).

coaching_recommendations: Turn the body first, arms second. Cue: “lead with your chest, not your hands.” Drill: make full turns using just the torso (no club), then reintroduce the arms so the body carries the arms through the finish (from p8_finish_faults.md: Arms-only finish).

Practice reaching a high, balanced finish with no ball. Make slow practice swings focusing entirely on wrapping the club high behind the lead shoulder and aiming at the target (not the ball) to reduce deceleration through impact (from p8_finish_faults.md: Short or low finish).

If balance is a problem, widen your athletic base and practice controlled, slowed swings holding the finish for three seconds. This highlights any instability and builds a repeatable, balanced finish position (from p8_finish_faults.md: Loss of balance at finish).

report.summary: This frame is a Finish (classifier confidence 99.98%). Two notable deviations stand out: an unusually high left-shoulder angle and a forward-tilted spine compared with typical pro ranges, consistent with an arms-dominant, under-rotated finish. These deviations match a recurring pattern seen earlier in this swing (previous finishes and toe-up showed persistent spine tilt), suggesting the body rotation is not completing and the arms are finishing the swing.

key_deviations.explanation: Left shoulder/arm finished much higher relative to pro norms — indicates the arms have wrapped to a high finish while the torso has not fully rotated (arms-only finish pattern).

Spine tilt remains well outside the pro range (more forward/away from expected finish tilt). Matches earlier frames' notable spine deviations, suggesting limited or incomplete body rotation through the swing.

coaching_recommendations: Address the arms-dominant finish: "Lead with your chest, not your hands." Practice making full torso-only rotations (no club) to ingrain the feeling that the body drives the arms — then add the club and let the torso carry the arms through to the finish. (source: p8_finish_faults.md)

Rehearse reaching a high, balanced finish: take slow practice swings without a ball, focusing on a full, wrapped finish behind the lead shoulder and holding the finish for 2–3 seconds. Progress to swings at 70–80% speed while maintaining that finish to avoid deceleration through impact. (source: p8_finish_faults.md)

If balance is a concern, widen and stabilize your athletic base at address and practice controlled swings until you can consistently hold the finish — this reduces the tendency to let the arms 'save' the swing and forces the body to rotate. (source: p8_finish_faults.md)

report.summary: The frame is a Finish with high classifier confidence. The torso shows an unusual backward tilt (spine_angle_from_vertical -10.9°) and the shoulder joint positions are well outside typical pro ranges, consistent with a finish where the arms have swung around a less-rotated body. This appears connected to earlier frames (Address and Toe-up) that also showed reduced/negative spine tilt, suggesting the limited body rotation is a persistent pattern through the swing.

key_deviations.explanation: Upper body is tilted backward relative to the pro typical finish — the torso remains closer to the address tilt instead of rotating upright through the finish, which is consistent with limited body rotation.

Right shoulder angle is far outside the pro interquartile range, indicating an unusual shoulder position at the finish that aligns with the arms doing much of the work while the body has under-rotated.

coaching_recommendations: Lead with the torso: practice torso-only rotations (no club) to ingrain turning the chest toward the target first, then add the arms. Cue from corpus: “lead with your chest, not your hands.” (drill from p8_finish_faults.md).

Finish-focused practice swings: take slow, no-ball swings concentrating on reaching a high, balanced finish aimed toward the target (think target, not ball). Replicate that feeling with the ball to discourage early deceleration or an arms-only wrap (recommendation from p8_finish_faults.md).

Balance and control drill: practice controlled 70–80% speed swings and hold the finish for three seconds; if balance fails, widen your athletic base and ensure weight is on the balls of the feet. This helps build stability so the body can rotate through the shot rather than the arms compensating (from p8_finish_faults.md).

report.summary: Frame classified as Finish (high confidence). The finish shows a notable forward spine tilt and large shoulder/arm angles that match an "arms-only finish" pattern — the torso appears under-rotated while the arms have swung around it. This is consistent with the earlier frames' repeated forward spine tilt and shoulder deviations, suggesting the issue is propagating through the swing.

key_deviations.explanation: Torso is more bowed/forward at the finish than typical pro ranges, indicating the body has not extended/rotated upright through the shot.
Shoulder/arm position is much higher/closed relative to pro ranges — consistent with the arms finishing around the body while the torso has under-rotated (an "arms-only" finish).

coaching_recommendations: Turn the body first, arms second — cue: “lead with your chest, not your hands.” (Drill: practice full turns with just the torso, then reintroduce the club.)
Practice reaching a high, balanced finish with no ball to train committing the body through the shot — think of the target, not the ball, and make practice swings focused on finishing high.
If balance is a concern, widen your athletic base and rehearse slow-motion swings holding the finish for 3 seconds; reduce speed to 70–80% until the balanced finish is repeatable.

synthesis.headline_summary: The swing shows a clear setup and posture pattern (reverse/forward-tilted spine at Address and early loss of posture at Toe-up) that persisted through impact and produced an arms-dominant, under-rotated finish — this will rob driver launch and consistency. A secondary but important issue is a likely open clubface at the toe-up position. Work first on setting a slight tilt away from the target at address and then on drills that force the torso to lead the arms through the finish.

priority_issues.issue_name: Reverse / forward spine tilt with under-rotation (arms-only finish)
priority_issues.explanation: Address shows a reverse spine tilt (spine_angle_from_vertical −6.2°) and a high trail shoulder, Toe-up shows further loss of forward bend (−9.8°), and every Finish frame records notably negative/outside pro-range spine angles (range approx. −13.4° to −8.1°) and shoulders consistent with an arms-only finish. The pattern indicates the body never tilted/rotated correctly away from the target at setup and then failed to turn through the shot, producing an arms-dominant follow-through and likely a downward/low driver strike with reduced launch and distance.
priority_issues.primary_recommendation: Begin by setting a small tilt away from the target at address using a club placed along the shoulders so the lead shoulder sits ~5–10° higher than the trail shoulder (Address drill). Immediately follow with torso-only rotation drills (no club) and slow no-ball swings where you 'lead with your chest, not your hands' — hold a high, balanced finish for 2–3 seconds (Finish/no-ball drills).

priority_issues.issue_name: Open clubface / shoulder rotation at Toe-up
priority_issues.explanation: The Toe-up frame shows a notable shoulder_line rotation (175°) and an estimated open face/shaft geometry inferred from lead-arm pose; this geometry commonly accompanies a face that is fanning open at the horizontal (toe-up) position and can lead to an open face at impact (push/fade or slice).
priority_issues.primary_recommendation: Work on a one-piece takeaway and allow natural forearm rotation with a neutral grip; practice arriving at Toe-up and visually check the leading edge so it finishes within ~15° of vertical (Toe-up drill).

beginner_report.encouragement: You have a very repeatable setup and clear swing shape to build from — that consistency is a huge advantage. Your shoulders and hips show reliable patterns, so a few targeted, simple changes should give noticeable improvements in driver launch and direction.

top_3_takeaways.title: Tilt slightly away at setup
top_3_takeaways.feel_cue: Feel your chest and lead shoulder tilt just a little away from the target so you’re leaning off the ball, not toward it.
top_3_takeaways.simple_drill: Place a club across your shoulders, raise the lead shoulder a touch higher than the trail shoulder, and make slow practice swings keeping that slight lean.

top_3_takeaways.title: Takeaway with your body
top_3_takeaways.feel_cue: Feel your shoulders and torso move the club back together so the hands don’t pull the club around and the face sits flatter when horizontal.
top_3_takeaways.simple_drill: On slow half‑swings stop at the horizontal, check the clubface, and practice taking the club back with your upper body rather than just your hands.

top_3_takeaways.title: Lead with your chest
top_3_takeaways.feel_cue: On the downswing feel your chest and hips start the turn toward the target first while your hands relax and follow.
top_3_takeaways.simple_drill: Do slow no‑ball swings where you start the downswing by rotating your chest toward the target and hold a balanced finish for 2–3 seconds.

beginner_report.one_sentence_summary: A consistent setup is letting you repeat the same swing, but a slight backward tilt at address and an open face mid-back combined with not letting your torso lead through the shot are causing an arms-led finish that cuts driver launch and consistency.
